pos.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, Ancelotti's Milan kept the ball through Pirlo, while his Real Madrid sides (2013-15, 2021-25) were happy to give it up and counter with Ronaldo, Bale and Vinicius, so possession is a tool, not a principle.

pro.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, his teams mix a deep-lying passer who breaks lines (Pirlo, Kroos, Modric) with fast, direct attacks after winning the ball, and he doesn't insist on playing out under pressure.

est.personaBrief: The verified shifts between the 4-3-2-1 'Christmas Tree' (Milan 2006-07) and the 4-3-3 (Madrid 2013-14) show a manager who fits the shape to his players; from general knowledge his attackers (Kaka, Benzema, Ronaldo, Vinicius) were allowed to roam rather than hold fixed zones.

lar.personaBrief: No verified evidence on width, but the verified 4-3-2-1 Christmas Tree at Milan played without wingers and filled the middle with playmakers; at Madrid the wide forwards cut inside rather than crossed.

blo.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, Ancelotti's teams, especially Madrid in 2013-14 and 2021-25, defended in a compact mid-to-low block and counter-attacked rather than pressing high.

mar.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, he comes from the Sacchi zonal school (Milan) and his teams defended zonally, with no dedicated man-markers on star players.

pla.personaBrief: The verified formation changes (Christmas Tree to fit Kaka, Seedorf and Pirlo; 4-3-3 at Madrid 2013-14) show him shaping the system around the squad he finds; from general knowledge he adapts to opponents rather than imposing a fixed model.

res.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, he is a pragmatic winner of trophies (five Champions Leagues) who manages games to protect results, more than a manager driven by spectacle.

sis.personaBrief: No verified evidence beyond formations built around his stars (the Christmas Tree for Kaka and Pirlo); from general knowledge he gives great players freedom and spares them some defensive duties, trusting talent over a rigid system.

jog.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, he made Pirlo a regista and built midfields of technicians (Seedorf, Kaka, Modric, Kroos), though he also accepts modern athletic demands.

bas.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, his title sides relied on experienced players (Milan's veterans, Madrid's Modric and Kroos), with young players like Vinicius brought in gradually; he is not an academy-builder.

lid.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, Ancelotti is the archetype of the calm man-manager who talks to his senior players, protects the group's mood and avoids iron-fist discipline.
